findings.current_state: Synergos: optimistic per-path u64 counter, conflict detected only for equal-version/different-content, no parent hash, no lock command, Phase 3 deferred. findings.proposed_redesign: Introduce a lock service with three layers. (1) Policy: a per-project `.synergos/policy.toml` (also mirrored as a Curare project setting) with typemap-style rules `[[rule]] match=["**/*.psd","**/*.uasset"] lock="exclusive"|"soft"|"none"`, applied at add time like P4 typemap. (2) State: Curare owns the authoritative `asset_locks` table `{logical_asset_id, resource_id, path, holder_user_id, device_id, destination_ref, state ∈ {held, retained, released}, acquired_at, expires_at}` exposed as an LFS-compatible API `POST /locks`, `GET /locks?path|refspec`, `POST /locks/verify`, `POST /locks/:id/unlock {force}` so Anchorpoint/Unreal/Unity LFS plugins work unchanged; Synergos gossips a signed `LockAnnounce{project, path, holder_peer, lock_id, exp}` and the publish path (ipc_server PublishUpdate) refuses to bump a locked path unless the local identity holds the lock. (3) Semantics: adopt Unity Smart-Lock 'destination branch + Retained' so a lock survives until the change lands on the destination ref; admin force-release writes an audit row and warns the next checker-out. Add `parent_hash` (BLAKE3 of the previous version) to FileOffer/TransferHeader/ManifestEntry so forks are detected even for soft-locked files; materialize the loser as `<name>.conflict-<peer>-v<N>` instead of dropping it. Client UX: set the read-only bit on lockable files (SVN needs-lock trick). 4軸: AI学習量=中 (LFS locking JSON + typemap are documented formats, no novel algorithm); 作業コスト=M (table+4 routes in Cu, one gossip message + publish gate + conflict-copy in Sy); 解決度=高 (closes lost-update for binaries, enables plugin compatibility); 主目的との一致度=高 (core promise 'アセットの競合が起きにくい' listed as Perforce's strength in spec/plan/competitive-analysis.md:23).

findings.current_state: Pull is fire-and-forget on every offer in an open project; receive compares only the last published/received record, never the on-disk bytes; sync_mode is decorative; conflict resolution is state-only; conflict copies (docs §4 Phase 3) are not implemented.

findings.current_state: Synergos: P2P manifest versions (path→u64, CRC32) with content-addressed history-node objects (BLAKE3). Curare: resource versions (uuid, SHA-256) stored in MinIO or Synergos custody under random blobRef keys; custody deliberately opaque. findings.proposed_redesign: Define one object identity and one manifest format across both repos. (1) Digest set: every version/object carries `digests: [{algo:'blake3', value}, {algo:'sha256', value}]` (Curare's planned digests[] in versioning-types.md:59-60); custody object key becomes the BLAKE3 digest so the same bytes are one object whether published by a daemon or uploaded by the Web UI (refcounted reclaim). (2) Manifest object: Synergos `.synergos/manifest.json` and Curare `manifests` (GW-03) are the same schema `{path → {blake3, size, parent, publisher, version}}`, content-addressed by its own BLAKE3; Curare stores manifest hashes, Synergos exports/imports them. (3) Bridge API: `POST /api/v1/projects/:id/manifests` (register a Synergos manifest as a Curare working snapshot; history node is the storage backend, no re-upload), `POST /api/v1/releases/:id/checkout-manifest` (emit a manifest the daemon can `project checkout --manifest`). (4) Custody becomes a history node role (same binary, `history.enabled` + HTTP capability surface) so there is one blob store with one retention policy. 4軸: AI学習量=中 (one schema, two serializers); 作業コスト=M〜L (digest migration is additive; custody re-keying needs a migration job); 解決度=高 (single truth, no double transfer, review/checkout round-trip); 主目的との一致度=高 (README promises Synergos handles transfer for Curare; today MinIO is the live path).
alternatives: Keep two systems but add a mapping table {synergos_project, path, version} → curare version_id and a 'promote from Synergos' command — cheaper, still two blob copies and two digests.
Drop Synergos projects entirely and make the daemon a Curare client (DCC common commands over IPC) — simplest story, loses P2P LAN fan-out for working trees.

findings.scenario: A remote artist on hotel Wi-Fi restores a 4 GB level from the history node. The QUIC connection idles 30 s during a Wi-Fi hiccup and dies (no keepalive), the TXFR stream restarts from byte 0, and because the restore pin expired after 5 min the arriving older version is rejected as stale. Switching to the Curare clone path: capabilities last 300 s, downloads are sequential, so after the first 5 minutes every remaining file 403s, refresh re-resolves the whole closure and re-issues N capabilities per file; closing the laptop lid aborts everything and nothing resumes at wake. Working offline is impossible on both sides: saves need Cernere per request, publishes need peers.
findings.impact_ai_game: Perforce/Plastic clients tolerate flaky links with resumable sync and local pending state; artists at home and outsourcers on slow links are the norm. AI jobs pulling 100 GB checkpoints need ranged, resumable, verifiable fetches (Xet/S3 range model).
findings.current_state: Sy: single-stream, no resume, no keepalive, pin TTL wall-clock, Queued transfers leak. Cu: single PUT/GET, no Range, 300 s GET, 24 h admission, per-file retry, Web IndexedDB journal only while open, Node CLI has no daemon.
findings.proposed_redesign: (1) Transport: set `keep_alive_interval` < idle/2 on both quinn configs; add resumable ranged transfer keyed by content hash (header `{blake3, offset, len}`) with a Bao outboard tree stored beside each history/custody object so any range verifies against the file hash; pins keyed to the in-flight transfer id, not wall clock. (2) Curare: HTTP Range + If-Range on custody/MinIO GET, multipart/tus-style PUT (IETF resumable-upload headers), per-item lazy capability issuance with renewal instead of bulk 300 s URLs, and a `GET /acquisition/plan/:id/renew` that re-signs without re-resolving the closure. Resume by re-admission only (current custody model) — no partial-byte resume; multi-GB files on slow links never complete (custody PUT has an 1800 s cap).

findings.scenario: Two level designers each publish a different OFPA actor file in the morning. Both daemons rewrite `.synergos/manifest.json` (pretty JSON, every entry's updated_at/version/crc changes) and both commit. The second `git push` is rejected; `git pull` produces a conflict in a machine-generated file with thousands of entries and no merge driver, so the designer hand-edits JSON or discards one side (losing the pointer to a published version). Separately, if both edit `Scenes/Main.unity` (Unity YAML) and git merges it with UnityYAMLMerge, Synergos still has two different v3 bytes for the same path and the loser's push is silently refused at debug level with no conflict copy.
findings.impact_ai_game: Unity scenes/prefabs and Unreal OFPA actors are text or many-small-file formats precisely so teams can merge; Unity ships UnityYAMLMerge as a git merge driver keyed by extension. A pointer manifest that itself conflicts on every parallel publish negates the 'git holds text' split (DVC's .dir files have the same problem, mitigated by one .dvc per directory).
findings.current_state: Single pretty-JSON manifest per project committed to git, rewritten whole on every publish/receive; no .gitattributes/merge driver; no per-directory manifests; conflicting text versions rejected without quarantine; TextDiff chain dormant.
findings.proposed_redesign: (1) Manifest layout: line-oriented, sorted, one entry per line (`path\tversion\tblake3\tsize`) or one manifest per directory, with a shipped `.gitattributes` (`.synergos/manifest.* merge=synergos-manifest`) and a `synergos git-merge-manifest %O %A %B` driver that unions entries and takes max(version)/newest-by-parent per path, flagging true per-path conflicts; `synergos project init` writes both files. (2) Merge-driver registry for text assets: `.synergos/policy.toml` `[[merge]] match=["**/*.unity","**/*.prefab"] driver="UnityYAMLMerge merge -p %O %B %A %A"` with premerge/fallback semantics; Synergos invokes it only for pinned conflict resolution (never auto-merge binaries), otherwise writes `<name>.conflict-<peer>-v<N>` (GW-02). (3) Include parent_hash in entries so the git-side merge can detect divergent lineage. 4軸: AI学習量=低 (git merge drivers are standard); 作業コスト=S for (1), M for (2); 解決度=高 for parallel publishing; 主目的との一致度=高 ('git はテキスト + manifest' is the chosen architecture).
alternatives: Stop committing the manifest; make the history node the index of record and export manifests only at release tags — contradicts the current 'index lives in git' decision but removes the conflict class entirely.
Keep one JSON but commit only from a single 'integration' node — operationally fragile.

findings.scenario: A tech artist reorganizes Textures/ into Textures/Characters/ (4 GB). Synergos treats every moved file as new: version 1 (or floor+1), full retransfer to every peer and history node (no content-hash dedup on the live path), and the old paths stay in every peer's working tree because checkout never deletes 'extra' files — a deleted placeholder asset resurrects on the next node that still offers it. In Curare, renaming a resource rewrites `name` in place, so release R1's items now display the new name and nobody can answer 'what was this file called when R1 shipped'.
findings.impact_ai_game: P4 `p4 move`, Plastic's move detection and git's rename heuristics keep history across reorganizations, which happen constantly in Unity/Unreal projects; datasets get re-sharded and re-labeled the same way. Without tombstones, 'delete this asset from the game' is not expressible.
findings.current_state: Sy: path-keyed entries, no tombstones, no hash, extras untouched. Cu: flat mutable name, no path, no rename history, id-only release snapshots.
findings.proposed_redesign: Make entries content-addressed with explicit ops. Synergos manifest entry gains `blake3` and `state ∈ {present, deleted}` (tombstone with version) and an optional `moved_from`; `project mv` and `project rm` IPC commands produce signed ops; receivers apply deletes to the working tree only with the dirty check (GW-02) and keep tombstones through GC grace; FileOffer carries blake3 so a rename is answered from local bytes without transfer (history node dedups by hash already). Curare: add `path` (unique per project per ref) to resources, record `{path, name}` on every `asset_versions` row and in submission items/release manifests (GW-03), add `POST /assets/:id/move` that writes a rename event instead of mutating in place, and an archive/delete op that writes a tombstone in the manifest rather than flipping visibility. 4軸: AI学習量=低〜中; 作業コスト=M (schema + 2 ops each side); 解決度=高; 主目的との一致度=高 ('what was shipped in R1' is a release-composition guarantee).
alternatives: Rename detection by hash only (no explicit op) — cheap on Synergos once blake3 is in the manifest, but still no delete semantics.
Keep names mutable but snapshot names into release.snapshot JSON — fixes the audit question only.

findings.scenario: A studio with a 1.5 TB Perforce depot (Warhorse scale) wants to adopt the platform. There is no `p4 → curare` importer, no way to record the original changelist number, submitter and timestamp on a version (createdBy must be the API caller's Cernere UUID, createdAt is now()), no bulk ingest (4 API calls + per-file Cernere WS auth per file), and no LFS compatibility so an existing LFS-based project cannot be re-pointed. The only option is to start history from zero.
findings.impact_ai_game: Every studio already has a VCS; migration cost decides adoption (Perforce's own positioning is 19/20 AAA). Hugging Face's Xet migration kept an LFS bridge for exactly this reason. AI teams likewise arrive with DVC/LFS repos.
findings.current_state: No importer, no external-revision metadata, no LFS batch/locks/pointer support, bulk ingest is per-file and auth-bound.
findings.proposed_redesign: (1) Metadata: add `origin{system: p4|svn|git-lfs|plastic, revision, changelist, author_name_hash?, submitted_at}` to asset_versions/manifest entries (hashed author, no PII) and allow trusted importers (service principal, GW-13) to set createdAt/origin. (2) Bulk ingest API: `POST /import/manifests` accepting a manifest (GW-03/GW-04) plus a batch admission (`POST /upload/batch` returning N capability URLs under one auth) so a 1M-file depot is ingested in manifest-sized units; history-node side `synergos history import --from p4 //depot/... ` streaming revisions into objects + index with origin tags. (3) Importers as CLI tools: `curare-import p4` (p4 filelog/print), `curare-import svn`, `curare-import lfs` (reads pointers + LFS objects), mapping branches/streams to refs; keep LFS wire compatibility (GW-07) so LFS-based teams can switch servers without rewriting history. (4) Dry-run report (files, bytes, dedup ratio by whole-file hash) before import. 4軸: AI学習量=中 (p4 filelog/svn dump formats are documented; LFS spec public); 作業コスト=M〜L; 解決度=高 for adoption; 主目的との一致度=中〜高 (external sale goal in use-cases.md:19-21 depends on it).
alternatives: Import latest state only (no history) — cheap, loses the archive that studios keep P4 for.
Run Synergos as an LFS custom-transfer/promisor behind an existing git+LFS host and skip Curare import — preserves git history for LFS teams only.

findings.scenario: A console project: 60 seats, 400k files, 3 TB. Curare: a milestone release of 2,000 approved assets cannot be finalized (closure cap 1000) and a single logical asset with 600 resources cannot be submitted (500); `GET /assets/:id/versions` returns every version of a PSD saved 50×/day; each of the ~5 API calls per file opens a Cernere WebSocket, so a 10k-file ingest is 50k handshakes. All org saves land on one custody node.
findings.impact_ai_game: Reference scale is public: Ubisoft 24M files/166M revisions/5 TB, Warhorse 1.5 TB/75 users; HF caps 10k entries per folder and 100k files per repo and still had to move to block-level CAS. The current ceilings exclude every console studio and most dataset work.
findings.current_state: Hard caps 500/500/1000; OFFSET pagination capped at 100 with unpaginated version/submission/assignment lists; O(n²) manifest/index rewrites; startup full scan; 1 MiB IPC; per-request WS auth; single storage node; no quotas.
findings.proposed_redesign: (1) Replace per-item caps with manifest objects (GW-03): submissions/releases reference a manifest hash, closure resolution becomes a set operation on manifest entries (recursive CTE + one grant query), acquisition plans are paged and lazily signed. (2) Cursor pagination on every list; `GET /versions?latest=1`. (3) Synergos: append-only manifest journal (one line per event) compacted into the committed manifest at publish/checkout boundaries, sqlite/redb for history index and version_state, lazy verification on first want with a size+mtime+inode cache instead of startup CRC. (4) IPC: streamed/paginated responses (`HistoryList{cursor}`) and a raised local frame cap. (5) Auth: short-TTL actor cache keyed by token hash with CAEP/SSF revocation hooks, request-time re-check only for destructive ops. (6) Storage topology: declared node roles (history/custody primary, replica, site cache) with per-org/site allocation and replication factor in receipts (P4 proxy/forwarding-replica/edge as one binary in modes). 4軸: AI学習量=中; 作業コスト=L overall (each item S〜M); 解決度=高 (unblocks real studios); 主目的との一致度=高.
alternatives: Raise the numeric caps to 50k and add indexes — buys time but keeps O(items) API bodies and per-file auth.
Keep one history node and accept startup scan — acceptable only for indie-scale projects.

findings.scenario: A World Partition level with 20,000 OFPA actor files is published to a 10-peer project: Synergos opens 20,000 FileOffer streams × 10 peers, then each peer sends 20,000 FileWant streams and receives 20,000 TXFR streams, each doing a manifest rewrite (GW-17). findings.impact_ai_game: OFPA is the default for new Unreal levels and ImageNet-style datasets are millions of small objects; S3's 100–200 ms first-byte makes per-object I/O the dominant cost, which is why HF caps files per folder and every CAS packs small blobs (Xet xorbs, WebDataset shards).
findings.current_state: Per-file everything on both sides; no batching of offers/wants, no packed small-object transfer, no batch admission, one catalog row pair per file.
findings.proposed_redesign: (1) Synergos: batch gossip — `FileOfferBatch{entries[]}` / `FileWantBatch` (≤ 256 KiB frame) and a `TXFR` pack mode that streams many small blobs in one QUIC stream with per-entry BLAKE3 (Bao-verified), driven by the manifest diff rather than per-file events; coalesce manifest writes per batch. (2) Curare: `POST /upload/batch` (one admission call → N capability URLs, one confirm with N hashes, one `POST /manifests` registering N versions) and a 'collection' resource kind whose versions are manifests (directory-as-asset) so an OFPA level or a dataset shard set is one logical asset with one row per version, not one per file. (3) Pack small blobs into xorb-like 64 MiB containers on history/custody nodes with a chunk-length table for ranged reads. 4軸: AI学習量=中; 作業コスト=M; 解決度=高 for OFPA/datasets; 主目的との一致度=高 (fast transfer is the main purpose).
alternatives: Only batch gossip (no pack transfer) — removes the n×m control streams, keeps n data streams.
Recommend Unity/Unreal users keep levels monolithic — contradicts engine defaults.
